page: Amazon Web Services r5dn.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor. The configuration delivers 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores at a 3.1 GHz clock frequency with support for AVX-512 vector extensions. System resources include 512.0 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, offering an 8.0 GB per-core allocation. Storage is provisioned via 2400 GB of local NVMe SSD instance store capacity, complemented by a 75 Gbps baseline network interface.

Benchmark data reflects strong memory and multi-core throughput, positioned alongside balanced general compute performance. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reached 224.73 GB/sec and write bandwidth achieved 98.73 GB/sec, placing both metrics in the top 25 percent. In PassMark testing, database operations scored 21799.59 and extended CPU instructions hit 54209.55, both placing in the upper tier. Multi-core performance is solid, evidenced by a multi-core stress-ng metric of 55948.23 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 12085.0. Single-thread processing remains lower, with single-core stress-ng and compression tasks placing in the bottom 25 percent.

The combination of high memory density, fast local NVMe storage, and 75 Gbps network bandwidth provides solid qualitative resource efficiency for data-intensive architectures. The primary architectural tradeoff centers on raw single-threaded performance versus aggregate memory capacity and I/O capability. The instance is suited for large in-memory databases, Redis caching clusters, high-throughput database operations, and distributed data processing systems requiring low-latency scratch storage.
description: Amazon Web Services r5dn.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, equipped with a 32-core, 64-vCPU Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz. It features 512.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing an 8.0 GB per-core ratio, paired with 2400 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage and a 75 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate exceptional large-block memory bandwidth exceeding 224 GB/sec read and 98 GB/sec write speeds, along with strong PassMark database operation scores. Single-threaded metrics are comparatively weaker, demonstrating that compute efficiency is geared toward parallelized workloads. The balance of massive RAM capacity, fast local ephemeral storage, and high networking throughput makes this configuration well aligned for memory-bound relational databases, in-memory caches, big data analytics, and high-performance transaction systems.
